newsitem.title: USA: NFL american football-FIVE-TIME PRO BOWL DE NEIL SMITH TO LEAVE CHIEFS.
newsitem.headline: NFL american football-FIVE-TIME PRO BOWL DE NEIL SMITH TO LEAVE CHIEFS.

text.p: Five-time Pro Bowl defensive end Neil Smith, who had hoped ot finish his career with Kansas City, will play for another team in 1997 after nine years with the Chiefs.
Smith, an unrestricted free agent, confirmed at a Friday news conference that the Chiefs decided not to re-sign him.
"I never thought it would end this way," Smith said.

"I thought that I would end my career here in Kansas City. I would love to end my career here, but it was a business decision," Smith said. "I have to live with it. I'm big enough and I'm old enough to handle it."
The 31-year-old Smith said he was told of the team's decision by Chiefs head coach Marty Schottenheimer Thursday.
"It was hard for me, a very emotional moment," Smith admitted. "I was hurt. I was crushed. But those things happen. This is a part of life."

Smith recorded just six sacks last season, half of his total from the previous year, which was a factor in Schottenheimer's decision. The outstanding defensive end has 86 1/2 sacks in his nine-year NFL career.
The Denver Broncos and Oakland Raiders, AFC West Division rivals of the Chiefs, have reportedly made offers to Smith.
"I have some offers," Smith said. "I've been to a lot of places. It's been a pretty interesting off-season for me."
The Chiefs last week acquired defensive lineman Brentson Buckner, a starter the past two seasons for the Pittsburgh Steelers, making Smith expendable.
